STATUS: fail SUMMARY: One reproduced [blocking] issue: when the focused element inside an open Dialog is removed, focus drops to body and Tab moves focus out of the modal, so the trap leaks. Most criteria held under about 60 probes across Tabs, Dialog, and Combobox. The remaining findings are minor edge cases (SSR tab stops, a spurious callback, README wording, and nested dialogs mounted together). FILES TOUCHED: src/__probe__.test.tsx (created for the probes and deleted; git status matches the start state) FINDINGS: - [blocking] Dialog focus trap leaks when the focused element is removed. Repro: focus a button inside the dialog, rerender without it, then press Tab. Result: `activeElement` is `BODY` after removal; after Tab it is `BUTTON outside`, not inside the dialog. Cause: the trap only acts on keydown whose target is inside the dialog, and a removed focus leaves the target on body. Fix idea: handle Tab on `document` while the dialog is open, or re-focus the dialog when focus leaves it. - [minor] Tabs uncontrolled with no defaultValue: after the adopted first tab is removed, no tab is `aria-selected` and the panel stays hidden. README says "With neither prop, the first enabled tab is selected." Reproduced: removing tab "a" left "b" with `aria-selected=false`, panel `hidden=true`. - [minor] Tabs SSR: `renderToString` with `defaultValue="b"` gives every tab `tabindex="-1"`, so no tab is reachable before hydration. Without a value, nothing is selected in the HTML. Not reproduced in a browser. - [minor] An arrow key on a single enabled tab calls `onValueChange("a")` again even though nothing changed. Reproduced: spy calls `[["a"]]` after ArrowRight. - [minor] Two nested Dialogs mounted in the same commit: the outer one's focus effect runs last and steals focus from the inner, so Escape closes the outer. Opening the inner later by click works correctly (inner closes alone). - [minor] README says Enter "shows its label"; with a parent that ignores `onChange`, the input clears to the old value's label (empty when null). Reproduced: Enter after ArrowDown left `""`. This follows controlled semantics, so the sentence should say so. - [minor] Combobox cannot be opened with a mouse click on the input (only typing or ArrowDown opens it). This matches the spec but is a discoverability gap; reproduced `aria-expanded="false"` after click. - [minor] `Dialog` with `description=""` still sets `aria-describedby` on an empty `

`. Reproduced; the spec says "when a description is given," so this is a judgment call. - [minor] Simplicity: Tabs uses layout-effect DOM scans plus a version counter bumped from every Tab; this is heavier than needed for the criteria. Not reproduced as a bug. CHECKS: - ArrowLeft/Right wrap, Home/End, first and last disabled, one enabled tab, dynamic insertion order, controlled-ignored, weird-character ids, id collision after encoding, StrictMode, two instances, className forwarding, preventDefault on arrow keys, disabled-click no-op, selected-value-matches-nothing tab stop → pass. - Dialog: portal and backdrop, aria-labelledby, describedby absent, initial focus (first focusable and container fallback), Tab/Shift+Tab wrap, Escape from nested input, backdrop click vs inside click, focus return on close/unmount/reopen/StrictMode, removed-trigger no-throw, no onOpenChange on mount, element added while open, disabled/tabindex=-1/hidden skipped, Escape on container, nested Escape (realistic order) → pass. - Dialog focus removal then Tab → fail (blocking above). - Combobox: label and attributes, typing filter case-insensitive, regex-special text, No results, arrow nav with disabled skip and wrap, Enter select, Enter with no active, click select, disabled click no-op, Escape restore, blur close, value prop sync, all-disabled, filter after active, clearing → onChange(null) once, duplicate labels by value, aria-selected/aria-disabled, options change while active, Escape inside Dialog (open listbox first, then dialog) → pass. - Combobox: "x.y*" substring and "(" filter → pass. - Not run: `pnpm test` and `pnpm typecheck` (the orchestrator ran them). OPEN QUESTIONS: - Should the Dialog focus trap also cover focus that has fallen to body (the blocking item)? The orchestrator needs to decide whether that is in scope for this round. - Should Combobox open on click? The spec only requires typing and ArrowDown.
